title: Porting from MV to MZ , is it worth it?

posts.author: iLLuvitar
posts.body:
Name states the intent; Basically I learned to code java script over the last two years during my free time whilst planning out a game I wanted to make. The more pertinent question is, how viable is this approach and should I bother? I have 'fusion' system plugin that is the fruit of my labor, and I take one actor and 'fuse' another actor with them, removing them from the party and tranferring a portion of their stats.
The plugin further more applies optionally applies states on fusion, and after the fusion is reversed and the player added back to the party. I dont own MZ as of yet, but I was told given the improvements to the engine it was generally preferred over MV which I DO own. Either way here is a, video show-casing the system in action. I would appreciate anyone's input on this one. I guess this post is mainly FOMO of the more recent engine since my game is not far along in development. Recommend speeding up the video btw.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
It boils down to:
MV: Cheaper, more plugins, the plugins are cheaper (Yanfly vs VisuStella). VS plugins are also obfuscated so you can't edit them and will run into compatibility issues with other plugins. Yes, there are alternatives to VS plugins but they are more niche and often when you ask how to do something you get recommended a VS plugin.
MZ: Better map editor, effekseeker for animations. Still gets support from the developer.

posts.author: iLLuvitar
posts.body: Gotcha. I'm not far along in development but I've done some tileset edits, and really the only yanfly plugin I 'rely' on is the item core that allows independent items. So it would really be too much of an issue if there's an alternative to the whole 'independent items' thing. My plugin was done with just the regular MV systems, cause I used it to learn and  brush up since covid.

posts.author: utunnels
posts.body:
A most frequently asked question.
There are very few plugins you can't port to MZ, and there are alternatives.
But, can't you finish your current project using MV? Is there a paticular reason why you decide to switch engine in the middle of the development?

posts.author: iLLuvitar
posts.body:
Well not quite the middle. I 'started' tentatively during covid and ended up doing a good bit of sprite edits and work on the 'fusion' mechanic I want to base my game around. There's really no world building establish, and things are still in the hazy phase. The main allure I suppose are the enhanced mapping capabilities and convenience mz affords with playing around with different icon / tile / portrait sizes.
